v.q: What happens to types in the emitted JavaScript?
o: They are checked at run time
v.w: The compiler checks and then removes them, so the runtime never sees a type.

v.q: Which data can TypeScript types not check by themselves?
v.w: Types are gone at run time, so external data needs a validator such as zod.

v.q: Which type forces you to narrow a value before using it?
v.w: any switches checking off. unknown accepts anything but must be narrowed.

v.q: What is the type of a function that always throws?
v.w: It has no return value at all, which is what never means.
An object with the required members fits the type, whatever its name.

v.q: What can an interface do that a type alias cannot?
v.w: Two interfaces with one name combine. Type aliases cover unions and computed types.

v.q: What makes a discriminated union narrow?
v.w: Checking the discriminant such as status tells the compiler which member it is.

v.q: What does assigning the leftover value to never in a switch do?
o: The build fails on a missing case
The value is cast to any
v.w: Add a new variant and forget its case, and the value is no longer never.

v.q: What does the constraint T extends HasId do?
o: Only types that have an id
It makes T a class type
It erases T at build time
v.w: The body can then use item.id safely.

o: The union of the keys of T
The values of T as an array
The class that T came from
v.w: With indexed access T[K] it types property lookups.

v.q: Which utility type makes all properties optional?
v.w: It is how update payloads are usually typed.

v.q: Which utility type removes some properties from a type?
v.w: Pick keeps chosen properties, Omit removes them.

v.q: What does value as Account check at run time?
v.w: It is a promise to the compiler, so a wrong shape fails later.

v.w: A value that may be missing must say so and be handled.

v.q: How do you type data from fetch safely?
o: Parse it as unknown and validate
Cast it with the as keyword
v.w: A zod schema validates at run time and derives the type.

v.q: Which is preferred over a TypeScript enum?
v.w: It erases cleanly, serialises naturally and has no generated code.
